Subject: Follow-up: pricing & committed-use discount

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — really helpful to see the latency numbers and how Redwood handles prefix caching. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we start budgeting:

- Expected monthly tokens: 50M input + 150M output (200M total) to start, ramping to ~1B tokens by Q4 with increased product rollout.
- Target unit economics: we need to get to <$600 per 1M tokens for this workload to make the ROI work in our model.
- Budget range: initially $8k–$12k/month, but with committed discounts we can push a larger upfront commitment if the unit price lines up.

We're also a Series A startup and would be interested in any startup program credits or multi-year incentives that could help during ramp. Can you share what committed-use tiers look like, and whether there's flexibility for multi-year discounts?

Looping in our finance lead, Sofia Ramos (cc), who will own the procurement side.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi Jordan — great speaking with you. Appreciate the clear numbers. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Recap of your ask:
- Current expected starting volume: ~200M tokens/month, plan to ramp to ~1B/month by Q4.
- Target price: <$600 per 1M tokens (your goal).
- Interested in startup credits + committed-use discounts and multi-year incentives.

Preliminary pricing and options (high level):
- On-demand hosted API (no commit): our standard list rate for similar models is usually in the $1,000–$1,600 per 1M tokens range depending on model family and sequence lengths.
- Committed-use (12 month): typical tiers give 20%–40% off on-demand depending on commit size. For example: $250k annual commit could get ~30% off compared to list.
- Multi-year commitment (2+ years): we can layer an additional 5%–10% incentive for multi-year contracts or prepay.
- Startup program: we have a startup credits program (one-time credits + steep initial discount window) — eligibility depends on stage and references; we can often combine credits with a smaller committed tier during first 6–12 months.

Ballpark math against your target ($600 / 1M):
- If list price = $1,200 / 1M, you need ~50% total reduction to hit $600. That level is achievable with a mix of committed-use + quantization/model guidance + startup credits during early months, but it requires a substantial commit (~$300k–$500k ARR equivalent) or multi-year prepay to reach the deepest bands.

Attachments: I attached a simple usage estimate template (Acme_usage_estimate_v1.xlsx) and our committed-use tier PDF (Redwood_committed_use_tiers.pdf) so you can see the mapping from commit sizes to discount bands.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether the 200M/month is a conservative starting bucket vs expected billing?
2) If possible, share an internal target range for annual commit ($) that your finance team would consider — we can build a concrete proposal.
3) We can put together a formal discount proposal and MOU once we have a target commit figure.

Ben/Aditya — can you add any perf/quantization notes that could materially affect unit economics for Acme's workload?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Jordan — quick technical note from the infra/SE side that should help pricing:

- Model choice & quantization: If your workload can run on a quantized 4-bit variant of the selected model family, we typically see 1.6–2x cost reduction at inference compared to full precision. That moves the effective list price down significantly.
- KV caching: because you mentioned many repeated prompts and prefix content, enabling prefix/KV caching can reduce effective tokens billed by ~10%–25% depending on reuse.
- Batching & routing: we can route non-latency-critical inference through lower-cost capacity tiers (dedicated shared bursts) to shave additional unit cost.

Operational suggestion: for a 200M/month starting point, I recommend a 12-month committed plan with quarterly review and a clause to scale up commit band after Q2 ramp. That structure paired with quantization could plausibly put you closer to the $600/1M target without needing the highest commit band up front.

I attached the committed-use tier PDF that Marissa referenced — happy to jump on a call to walk Sofia through the technical tradeoffs.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful. Sofia and I reviewed internally and a few clarifying items:

- The 200M/month is our conservative starting forecast; realistic plan is to budget for 300M/month to avoid surprise overages while we ramp.
- Our CFO (Sofia) is open to a 12-month committed plan in the $200k–$350k ARR range if we can lock closer to $600/1M effective pricing in Year 1 (credits + commit).
- Multi-year option: Sofia asked whether a 2-year commit with a 10% additional incentive and an option to increase commit at year-1 renewal is something Redwood would entertain.

Request: can you share a formal proposal with 2 options: (A) 12-month commit at $200k ARR showing effective $/1M tokens with credits/quantization assumptions; (B) 24-month commit at $350k ARR with multi-year incentive baked in and an option to scale commit after 12 months.

If you can get that over by EOD Friday (2027-03-19), Sofia wants to review and, if acceptable, move to contracting.

Thanks — Jordan
